details:
* SECURITY UPDATE: Destination-tree escape via symlink following in
     --relative implied-parent handling
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-53785.patch: resolve the receiver's destination
       names one component at a time with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY, acting
       against a directory fd that is held open, instead of handing the whole
       name to the kernel to resolve; a component that is a symlink is now
       refused rather than traversed, so nothing the receiver creates lands at
       the symlink's target outside the destination tree; adds
       secure_relative_dirfd(), do_mkdir_at(), do_stat_at(), do_open_at(),
       do_rename_at(), do_symlink_at(), do_mknod_at() and do_link_at() in
       syscall.c and routes every way the receiver creates something at a
       destination name through them -- make_path() in util.c, the four
       implied-parent sites in generator.c, the install-into-final-name
       renames in util.c, rsync.c, receiver.c and generator.c, copy_file()'s
       reopen of the destination on the cross-filesystem fallback, the
       symlink and mknod creations in generator.c's atomic_create(), and the
       --link-dest and -H hard links in generator.c and hlink.c; each of
       those is its own route to the destination name, reached by a different
       option (--temp-dir bypasses the file create entirely, --devices /
       --specials and a transferred symlink never touch it, and --link-dest
       installs a regular file's link from hlink.c but a non-regular file's
       from generator.c), so confining only some of them leaves the escape
       open; extends the existing secure_mkstemp() and secure_relative_open()
       receiver create paths, which the CVE-2026-29518 fix gated on
       daemon-no-chroot only, to the same confinement; the confinement covers
       a chrooted daemon serving an inner-module "/./" boundary, whose module
       root the kernel chroot does not confine, and exempts --keep-dirlinks
       only for a local receiver, whose documented purpose is to follow a
       symlinked destination directory -- never for a daemon or for the
       server side of a push, where the option arrives from the peer; only
       the confinement this CVE needs is carried, not upstream's whole-tree
       dirfd-stack resolver, which assumes a source layout this version does
       not have; defines am_daemon, am_chrooted, am_server, local_server and
       keep_dirlinks in t_stub.c, which the standalone test harnesses link in
       place of options.c and main.c, so debian/rules' check target still
       builds; and adds testsuite/cve-2026-53785.test
     - CVE-2026-53785
